metadata.title: A Conditional Reduction of the 4D Pure Yang–Mills Mass Gap — Second Edition: The Wall in Two Coordinates
metadata.description:
Status. This is a conditional reduction and an audit, not a proof of the Clay problem. The mass gap for 4D pure SU(N) Yang–Mills remains open. Clay = 0%. No step of this paper is labelled QED.

What the paper does. It rewrites the gap as the statement that the Källén–Lehmann spectral measure of tr F2 has a positive, isolated atom at the bottom of its support; proves the exact squeeze f12/χ ≤ inf supp ν ≤ M0/χ, so that a mass lower bound needs both a residue floor and a susceptibility ceiling; and shows that H1 (χ ≤ 1/λ) is necessary but not sufficient because it is blind to a thin atom. The countermodel is machine-checked in Lean 4 (module H1Sharpening, zero sorry). A conditional theorem with machine-verified gluing lemmas is stated, and the no-gos and exact missing steps are recorded.

New in the second edition. Part III draws the same obstruction in two independent coordinates. (a) Measure / weak-*: the atom is exactly the weak-* discontinuity of the boundary density; finite data are weak-* continuous and atomless measures are weak-* dense, so any forcing functional must be discontinuous — either a reading or an infinite-data limit (H1). (b) β/RG/conformal: the gap is equivalent to pure Yang–Mills (Nf=0) lying outside the conformal window. The window is real (SU(3) with 9 ≤ Nf ≤ 16 is asymptotically free and gapless-conformal), so asymptotic freedom alone does not imply a gap; no exact identity forbids an infrared fixed point; eight modern β/CFT routes fail, each for a sharp reason.

Ledger. Positively: a strong-coupling residue theorem (f12 > 0 for β < 1/48, volume- and L-uniform; I1, not I2); a kinematic no-dissolution theorem; Wgeo ≥ 0 by Prékopa; gauge-invariant Perron–Frobenius and its edge no-go; the coarse Poincaré lemma; the Feshbach–Bogoliubov two-block lemma; the exact variance decomposition G″ = S − D; the residue–level-gap lemma; and a machine-checked conditional theorem. Negatively: the Schur-convex master obstruction, Goldstone uniqueness, the periodic, nested-cone, rigidity, Feshbach-angle and Krein no-gos; the elimination of the order-parameter, topological-index and Markov-functional paradigms; and a structural no-go for complex-function-theory forcing tools (the Hardy L2 functional detects presence but not weight).

Verdict. The wall did not fall; it became transparent, ruled, instrumented, and drawn twice. What is missing is one object: a nonperturbative, non-circular, sign-controlling, free-field-failing, cutoff-uniform upper bound on a conditioned variance — equivalently a nonperturbative sign theorem for βNf=0. Naming it precisely is the paper's real result.
metadata.notes: Second edition (v2), 81 pages. Supersedes the 31-page v1 (DOI 10.5281/zenodo.24486316). Not a proof: Clay remains open. New in v2: Part III (two independent coordinates: measure/weak-* and beta/RG/conformal); machine-checked H1 sharpening; Savvidy false obstruction removed; tool-wave classification; lattice diagnostics; verification map; errata (free-vector a/c corrected to 31/18). Clay = 0%; no QED.
